input_references.role: Independent west-Jutland coastline reference for coastal distance analysis
West-Jutland coastal harbours used by recurrent offshore excursions

metadata.goal: Analyze how tourist vessel movement patterns vary across time and different coastal operating areas.
metadata.dataset_description: Constructed tourist-vessel movements along the west-Jutland coast over one Monday-to-Sunday week: the nearshore majority follows coast-parallel excursion paths, while seven recurrent vessels make longer offshore trips connected to several coastal harbour areas.
metadata.source_note: Danish maritime geography is used as context; the visible trajectories and attributes are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Tourist vessel activity increases during weekend daytime periods, with departures spanning a wider portion of the day than on comparable weekdays.

plot.title: Tourist-vessel Activity by Time

import pandas as pd
df=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); x=df.query('distance_to_coast_km >= 0.10 and point_index >= 3').copy(); s=x.groupby(['trajectory_id','trajectory_coast_band']).agg(speed_sd_knots=('sog_knots','std'),mean_delta_cog_15min_deg=('delta_cog_15min_deg','mean')); print(s.groupby(level=1).median())

insights: Tourist vessel activity increases during weekend daytime periods, with departures spanning a wider portion of the day than on comparable weekdays.
Most tourist vessels remain close to the coastline, while a smaller recurring group makes longer offshore trips to and from coastal harbour areas.
